From d10a26aa4d072320530e6968ef945c8c575edf61 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Martin Schiller <ms@dev.tdt.de>
Date: Tue, 31 Mar 2026 09:43:17 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] net/x25: Fix potential double free of skb

When alloc_skb fails in x25_queue_rx_frame it calls kfree_skb(skb) at
line 48 and returns 1 (error).
This error propagates back through the call chain:

x25_queue_rx_frame returns 1
    |
    v
x25_state3_machine receives the return value 1 and takes the else
branch at line 278, setting queued=0 and returning 0
    |
    v
x25_process_rx_frame returns queued=0
    |
    v
x25_backlog_rcv at line 452 sees queued=0 and calls kfree_skb(skb)
again

This would free the same skb twice. Looking at x25_backlog_rcv:

net/x25/x25_in.c:x25_backlog_rcv() {
    ...
    queued = x25_process_rx_frame(sk, skb);
    ...
    if (!queued)
        kfree_skb(skb);
}

Fixes: 1da177e4c3f4 ("Linux-2.6.12-rc2")
Signed-off-by: Martin Schiller <ms@dev.tdt.de>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260331-x25_fraglen-v4-1-3e69f18464b4@dev.tdt.de
Signed-off-by: Paolo Abeni <pabeni@redhat.com>

diff --git a/net/x25/x25_in.c b/net/x25/x25_in.c
index b981a4828d08..0dbc73efab1c 100644
--- a/net/x25/x25_in.c
+++ b/net/x25/x25_in.c
@@ -44,10 +44,9 @@ static int x25_queue_rx_frame(struct sock *sk, struct sk_buff *skb, int more)
 	if (x25->fraglen > 0) {	/* End of fragment */
 		int len = x25->fraglen + skb->len;
 
-		if ((skbn = alloc_skb(len, GFP_ATOMIC)) == NULL){
-			kfree_skb(skb);
+		skbn = alloc_skb(len, GFP_ATOMIC);
+		if (!skbn)
 			return 1;
-		}
 
 		skb_queue_tail(&x25->fragment_queue, skb);
 
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of the Patch

The patch fixes a potential double-free bug in the X.25 networking stack (`net/x25/x25_in.c`). The issue occurs when `alloc_skb()` fails inside `x25_queue_rx_frame()`: the function was freeing the `skb` and then returning an error, but the caller (`x25_backlog_rcv()`) would also free the same `skb` upon receiving the error, leading to a double free.

### Modifications in Each File

- **`net/x25/x25_in.c`**: In the `x25_queue_rx_frame()` function, the error handling branch for a failed `alloc_skb()` was changed. The `kfree_skb(skb)` call was removed, and the function now returns `1` without freeing the `skb`. This ensures that the caller is solely responsible for freeing the `skb` on failure.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The single change in `x25_queue_rx_frame()` eliminates the premature `kfree_skb(skb)` on `alloc_skb` failure. By allowing the error to propagate upward without freeing the packet, the caller (`x25_backlog_rcv()` in the same file) will correctly handle the error and free the `skb` only once (via its own `kfree_skb(skb)` when `queued == 0`). This resolves the double-free vulnerability.
